Otter

Otters are carnivorous mammals in the subfamily Lutrinae. The 13 extant otter species are all semiaquatic, aquatic, or marine, with diets based on fish and invertebrates. Lutrinae is a branch of the Mustelidae family, which also includes weasels, badgers, mink, and wolverines, among others.

Otters have a very soft, insulated underfur, which is protected by an outer layer of long guard hairs. This traps a layer of air close to the skin, keeping them dry, warm, and somewhat buoyant under water. Several otter species live in cold waters and have very high metabolic rates to help keep them warm.

  • Giant otter
  • European otter
